senses.gloss: (h. זֶה, cmp. דֵּין; corresp. to h. אֲשֶׁר, שֶׁל, שֶׁ־)who, which, where, whom &c.
units: Targ. Ps. LXXIII, 27; a. fr.—Mostly as prefix: דִּי־, דִּ־, דְּ־, v. דְּ־.—With personal pronouns דִּידִי, דִּילִי; דִּידָךְ, דִּידֵיךְ, דִּילָךְ, דִּילִיךְ; דִּידֵיה, דִּידָהּ, דִּילֵיה, דִּילָהּ; דִּידָן, דִּילָן; דִּידְכוֹן, דִּלְכוֹן, דִּידְכוּ, דִּידְכֶן; דִּידְהוֹן, דִּידְהוּ, דִּידְהִי mine, thine &c.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 31:16">Targ. O. Gen. XXXI, 16</cite> <he>דילנא</he> (Y. <he>די לנא</he>). Targ. O. ib. XXXIII, 9; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 4b:2">B. Bath. 4ᵇ</cite> <he>דידי ודידיה הוא</he> it is mine and his.
Ib. עבד דידיה he made the ḥazith on his side, v. חָזִית.
Ber. 2ᵇ בין השמשות דידך thy definition of ben hash-sh’mashoth.
<cite ref="Tamid 32a:51">Tam. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>דידי טבא מדידכו</he> my advice is better than yours.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 117b:3">B. Kam. 117ᵇ</cite> <he>דילכון אמרי דילהון היא</he> I believed (learning) was yours (the Palestineans’); but it is theirs (the Babylonians’); <cite ref="Sukkah 44a">Succ. 44ᵃ</cite> <cite ref="D00839"><he>דִּלְכוֹן</he></cite>, <cite ref="D00839"><he>דִּלְהוֹן</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Chullin 42b:1">Ḥull. 42ᵇ</cite> <he>תנא דידן</he> the author or compiler of our Mishnah.
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2">Deut. R. s. 2</cite> <he>ר״י דידיה אמר</he> R. J. said in his own name.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 17a:6">Ab. Zar. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>פליגא דידיה אדידיה</he> there is a discrepancy between two opinions of his.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:2:6">Y. Ḥag. II, 78ᵃ</cite> top <he>מן דידכֶן</he>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 6:6:5">Y. Snh. VI, 23ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>מן דידכון</he> one of yours.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:1:11">Y. Taan. IV, 67ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>די תעניתא</he> that it is a fast-day.
